To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified the binding site of Zn2+ that allosterically enhances agonist binding to the β2 adrenergic receptor.
Zn(II), a metal that is abundant in biological systems, is a positive allosterite modulator of the agonist affinity of the β2AR.
Zn2+ allosterically modulates agonist affinity in β2 adrenergic receptors and that this allosteric binding site is located between TM5 and TM5 and TM 5 and TM 6.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of allosteric modulation of the β2 adrenergic receptor by Zn2+.
the identification and characterization of the allosteric site for Zn2+ in the β2-adrenegic receptor.
the identification of allosteric binding sites in the β2-adrenoceptor and the mechanism by which Zn(II) modulates agonist affinity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Zn2+ binds to His-269 and Glu-265 and Glut-225 and stabilizes a conformational change that is required for agonist binding.
Zn2+ binds in the hydrophilic groove formed between TM5 and TM7, and that this binding site is allosterically linked to the orthosteric binding site.

Zn(II), by interacting with the cytoplasmatic extension of TM5 and/or TM6, facilitates agonist-induced conformational rearrangements in these domains, which are necessary to stabilize the active state of the β2AR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Zn2+ acts as an allosteric modulatory ligand by bridging two transmembrane domains and thereby facilitating the agonist induced conformational change required for receptor activation.
the Zn2+-mediated enhancement of agonist binding to the β2AR is allosteric and that it occurs via bridging of the intracellular ends of TM5 and 6.
the binding of an allosteric ligand to an allosteric binding site in the β2-adrenoceptor can modulate the affinity and/or efficacy of an agonist by altering the relative orientation of TM5 and TMS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
allosteric ligands may be able to modulate the affinity for agonist by binding at sites that are distant from the orthosteric site.
allosteric ligands may act by binding at sites that facilitate the conformational changes necessary for agonist binding.
the allosteric site for Zn2+ on the β2AR is not located in a single hydrophilic loop, but rather in a hydrophilic sequence that connects two transmembrane helices.
